name: Windows Blue
lede: Windows Blue is the mid blue of Microsoft's Windows desktop, a commercial name that entered color lists only in the 2010s.

sections.title: A desktop blue
sections.body:
The name is a software one: our library files it as the default desktop blue of Microsoft Windows, and it reaches color lists through the xkcd survey of 2010 [1]. The swatch is a vivid blue, about 4.7 units from the ISCC-NBS name vivid blue [1].

The color books we searched say nothing about it. The one hit in the concordance is a passage about stained-glass windows in Thuringia, where madder merchants are said to have persuaded glaziers to make church-window devils blue to discredit woad, which only shares the word *windows* [2]. It is not about this color.

sections.title: What the archive shows
sections.body: A blue this clear appears in 27 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, mostly as an accent: 77% of the 13 paintings where it is measured within the painting [3]. The earliest match is a 1426 Fra Angelico, a look-alike hue and not a Microsoft connection [3]. With so little sourced history, the honest summary is a brand-era name for an ordinary vivid blue next to [[azure]] and [[cobalt-blue]] [1].

origin.named_after: the Microsoft Windows default desktop background

notes.cite: St Clair, The Secret Lives of Colour, "Blue" (concordance hit on the word windows)

questions.q: Where does Windows Blue first appear in our color sources?
True or false: the color books we searched tell a history of Windows Blue.

openers: Windows Blue enters color lists in 2010, not in any pigment book.

issues: Reworded St Clair stained-glass anecdote to match source (madder merchants persuaded glaziers to make devils blue)
